report.source_text: CT with contrast showed a hypervascular 3.4 x 4.7 x 6.1 cm mass that extended from the nasal cavity to the oropharynx (Figures 2A-2F). The left maxillary sinus demonstrated erosion of the medial wall, making it the likely site of origin. Posterior maxillary sinus bowing (Holman-Miller sign) was not noted and the pterygopalatine fossa and pterygomaxillary fissure were not widened, making JNA less likely. All of the paranasal sinuses demonstrated mixed attenuation accumulation of fluid except for the right frontal and right superior ethmoidal sinuses, likely reactive. Left-sided cervical lymphadenopathy was also noted.

clinician.final_diagnosis: angiomatous inflammatory nasal polyp with no malignancy identified
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 16-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of epistaxis, nasal obstruction, foul-smelling nasal discharge, bilateral polyposis, and a soft palate mass. Physical exam confirmed bilateral polyposis and a soft palate mass causing uvula displacement. CT imaging revealed a large hypervascular mass (3.4 x 4.7 x 6.1 cm) extending from the nasal cavity to the oropharynx, originating from the left maxillary sinus with erosion. Imaging ruled out juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. Nasopharyngeal biopsies demonstrated granulation tissue and necrotic tissue with bacterial colonies but no malignancy. Angiography identified tumor blush from the distal left internal maxillary artery; preoperative embolization was successfully performed. Despite no available final surgical pathology report disclosed, the prior biopsy and clinical/imaging findings support a diagnosis of angiomatous inflammatory nasal polyp without malignancy.
